data.ruling: The refutation stands for the watchdog half of the figure. The RUN and brownout half of the figure is correct. Held in reset by RUN or by a brownout, the pads are output high-impedance and pulled low at 36 to 113 kΩ at IOVDD = 3.3 V. The watchdog half is wrong. It says the datasheet leaves the level open because the isolation latches hold each pad through a watchdog reset. The latches hold a pad only while its ISO bit is set, and gpio_set_function() clears that bit. On a pad with ISO clear, a reset of the PADS block returns the pad to its reset state, and a watchdog reset does not set ISO again. Whether a watchdog reset resets PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 depends on the firmware's PSM_WDSEL and RESETS_WDSEL settings, both 0x0 at reset. The SDK's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC. That includes RESETS (bit 4). RESETS then returns to its reset value, which holds PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) in reset (0x1). So under the SDK's watchdog configuration, a gated line goes to high impedance, pulled low, through a watchdog reset. The same low holds under RUN and brownout. The level is set by the firmware's WDSEL settings, not by the latches. The figure has to be restated on that basis. The refutation concerns the V73 requirement figure, not the RP2354B as a part. Its scope is therefore the function.
data.evidence:
Evidence re-read in the RP2350 datasheet (build-date 2025-07-29).

- Section 9.3 (p. 588): the pads return to the reset state on a brownout reset, on RUN held low, on SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and on an RP-AP rescue reset. The reset state is output buffer high-impedance, input disabled, pulled low, isolation latched. Also: "If a pad's isolation latches are in the latched state ... resetting the PADS and IO registers does not physically return the pad to its reset state." The IMPORTANT note says gpio_set_function() clears GPIO0.ISO.
- Section 9.7 (p. 596): the latches hold output enable, output level and pull enables only "when the ISO bit for each pad is set ... or the switched core domain is powered down". Also: "The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads."
- Section 7.4: "Following a watchdog reset trigger, the PSM restarts from a point selected by the PSM WDSEL register."
- Table 532 (PSM WDSEL): bit 4 is RESETS, reset value 0x0.
- Table 535 (RESETS: RESET): bit 9 PADS_BANK0 and bit 6 IO_BANK0 both reset to 0x1.
- Table 536 (RESETS: WDSEL): every bit resets to 0x0.
- Section 12.9.4: PSM_WDSEL, RESETS_WDSEL and POWMAN_WATCHDOG set the watchdog's reset level.
- Section 12.9.6.1, SDK _watchdog_enable, lines 52 and 53: "Reset everything apart from ROSC and XOSC", hw_set_bits(&psm_hw->wdsel, PSM_WDSEL_BITS & ~(PSM_WDSEL_ROSC_BITS | PSM_WDSEL_XOSC_BITS)).
- Table 1436: pull-down resistance at IOVDD = 3.3 V is 36 kΩ minimum, 113 kΩ maximum.

A search of the checkout's .c and .h files outside tools/ found no watchdog_enable, psm_hw or wdsel. The WDSEL setting the board's firmware will use is not stated in the tree.
